P.h: Max-severity GitLab flaw exploited against Alpine Linux
P.p: A CVSS 10 flaw in Ruby's Onigmo regex engine lets unauthenticated attackers run code through crafted GitLab CI/CD configurations. Attackers hit Alpine Linux on October 20 to 21, crashed worker processes and downloaded its container image. CISA added the bug to its KEV list.
P.s: Alpine found no confirmed code execution or repository tampering, rebuilt the instance and reset passwords. GitLab-only updates may not be enough for custom Ruby deployments: use Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9 or later.

items.h: Backdoored Claude VS Code extension sat on Cursor for nearly 12 hours
items.d: Version 2.1.313 went out through Anthropic's official Cursor account, targeting up to 5,000 developers. It tried to add an SSH key and open a reverse tunnel. Check indicators if you updated Thursday.

items.h: Binance resumes withdrawals after record $6.3B hack
items.d: The FBI attributes it to North Korea-linked TraderTraitor. A compromised laptop and evidence-deleting malware were involved. Binance has replenished 90% of stolen assets. TLDR also ran the inside story of the response.

items.h: Hijacked DebugBear script drains about $2.7M from Polymarket traders
items.d: The script abused signed-in sessions on October 29, moving funds from 33 wallets in 52 minutes. The compromise began at DebugBear's domain registrar. Polymarket is refunding $3.9M.

items.h: Linux TCP use-after-free: Ubuntu and RHEL still unpatched
items.d: A CVSS 9.8 bug reachable with one SYN, but the only known exploit needs an MPTCP listener, and Go 1.24+ programs open them by default. Debian, Amazon Linux and Oracle UEK have patches.

P.h: AI agents now run real intrusions and rank victims by value
P.p: Google and Mandiant saw intruders feed stolen credentials to the open-source ARTEX framework, whose six sub-agents ran cloud permission sweeps, Kerberoasting and DCSync. One suspected PRC-nexus cluster went from a first account to deep access in about four hours. The agents were noisy and sometimes undid each other's work.
P.s: Talos says the VOLTA infostealer steals everything, then sends the dossier to Claude, with Kimi and Gemini as fallbacks, for a ranked 'what they're worth' score. Defenders: short-lived scoped credentials, and alert when non-developer processes launch headless Chrome.

tiles.t: ChatGPT accounts taken over with one link
tiles.d: A MathLive keyboard feature plus HTML Preview escaped the sandbox and ran as chatgpt.com. OpenAI fixed it October 26 as P1. TLDR DevOps.
Codex plus Binary Ninja found hardcoded keys in minutes. Hidden accounts used passwords like 123456.

tiles.t: Applebee's app shipped a database password

P.h: AI bug reports push Postgres 19 past its release window
P.p: A surge of AI-assisted bug reports and patches has pushed PostgreSQL 19 late. Maintainers still have to verify each proposed fix and apply it to older versions. The project now targets November 19 for release.
P.s: The general TLDR edition adds that several large features were reverted late in beta, and that AI made finding bugs easier, which pulled focus from new features because the project prioritizes quality.

P.h: Datadog says serverless should be the default for AI agents
P.p: Datadog argues teams should evaluate serverless first for AI agents. It cites a study of more than 35,000 coding agent sessions in which LLM or tool calls filled only 20% of the median session, so idle time dominates.
P.s: Google Cloud's companion post says GKE Dataplane V2 avoids Cilium's 65,536 identity limit for dense agent workloads and reports 300 sandboxes per second at sub-second latency.
